mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS exceeds 100,000 monthly increases triggers a confidence effect that accelerates S&P 500 gains over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In a contractionary labor market regime (UNRATE > 6%), the correlation between PAYEMS acceleration and 20-day SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a shift from supply-side to demand-side easing, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >10% while INDPRO decreases by >5% in the same month
failure_condition: Over 20 consecutive 5-day windows, no consistent positive return is observed when the HOUST/INDPRO pattern recurs (average return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below 110 for three months suggests persistent supply-side weakness, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: During a supply-side recovery period (INDPRO crosses above 110), the predicted negative returns do not materialize (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months, it signals a labor market softening that reduces the real discount rate, thereby supporting higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% and remains below for two months
failure_condition: In a tightening regime (UNRATE > 4.5% for 3 months), the UNRATE crossing below 4% does not precede a statistically significant positive 60-day SPX return (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of job growth exceeding 150,000 (PAYEMS) while the unemployment rate remains below 4% creates a momentum signal that predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In regimes where unemployment is rising (UNRATE trend up), the interaction does not produce a statistically significant positive return (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in consumer spending momentum (HOUST) followed by a sharp decline in the goods price index (CPIAUCSL) suggests demand is shifting from inflation-sensitive to value-oriented, predicting positive 20-day SPX returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >15% while CPIAUCSL decreases by >2% in the same month
failure_condition: Over 10 windows, the pattern recurs but returns are not statistically positive (mean return ≤ 0).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS is above 4.5% and UNRATE is below 5%, a contrarian signal is generated that predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
regime_hint: contrarian policy and labor market conditions
failure_condition: The signal is triggered more than 30% of the time but produces positive returns in >50% of instances (p < 0.05 for the opposite sign).
